html:
A rail tunnel about 50 kilometres long under the English Channel, linking Folkestone in England with Coquelles near Calais in France. It was dug from 1988 and opened in May 1994. Its undersea section is the longest in the world.

Plans for a tunnel go back to the time of Napoleon, and work actually began in the 1880s, but British fears of invasion stopped it. In 1986 Margaret Thatcher and François Mitterrand agreed to build it with private money. Teams of tunnel boring machines dug from both sides through a layer of chalk marl, and they met under the sea in December 1990.

It has two rail tunnels and a service tunnel between them. It carries Eurostar passenger trains between London, Paris and Brussels, shuttle trains with cars and lorries, and freight. Queen Elizabeth II and Mitterrand opened it together.

It cost far more than planned, and the operating company struggled with debt for years. But it ended Britain's separation from the continent by land for the first time since the Ice Age, when Britain was joined to Europe.
